===Maruna-Kurina's Notes===
Oh, you've heard of Maat? A regular living legend, that one. He's been living in Jeuno since it was no more than a flyspeck of a fishing village-willage. They say he's mastered every form of combataru there is!
I've run into him before in North Gustaberg. But rumor has it he is in charge of some very important tasks back at the Grand Duchy. I wonder how he finds the time to go for leisurely strolls so far away...
He has a rival too, you know? What was his name again... Hegen...no...Degenhard! That's it! He's been known to wreak havoc-wavoc on the battlefield every now and then.
He loves collecting those ancient papyrus testimonies, no matter what variety. He also has a penchantaru for ambitious souls, and is said to dote on those who have mastered three or more paths of their own. 

===How to Influence===
*Trade [[Category:Testimonies|testimonies]] to influence him. (He will accept already used and worn testimonies also).
**Maat will not accept any testimonies for the jobs that he is not directly involved in breaking ([[Blue Mage]], [[Corsair]], [[Puppetmaster]], [[Dancer]], [[Scholar]]). You will get the correct dialogue for influence but he will not take the test or gain any influence by it.
*According to the clues given by [[Maruna-Kurina]], it may be possible to influence him by speaking directly if you have completed 3 or more of the [[Shattering Stars]] limit break quests that involve fighting him. {{Verification}}
''"What's this...? Interesting...No, no. I'm sorry, youngster. I don't have time for that now. But maybe someday when this war is over..."''

After a 10,000 [[Gil]] of stock has been purchased, she will change her stock immediately and will offer the following:
*[[Uleguerand Milk]] : 150 gil
*[[Chalaimbille]]: 300 gil
*[[Cheese Sandwich]]: 800 gil
*[[Bavarois]]: 3,360 gil
*[[Cream Puff]]: 1,300 gil
*[[Wormy Broth]] : 100 gil

After even more of her stock has been purchased (roughly 250,000 gil plus the losses, see note below) she will change her stock again after 1 hour wait and she will offer the following:
*[[Uleguerand Milk]] : 100 gil
*[[Chalaimbille]]: 250 gil
*[[Cheese Sandwich]]: 800 gil
*[[Bavarois]]: 3,360 gil
*[[Cream Puff]]: 1,300 gil
*[[Buffalo Milk Case]]: 5,000 gil
*[[Buffalo Meat]]: 1,280 gil
*[[Enfire II]]: 31,878 gil
*[[Enblizzard II]]: 30,492 gil
*[[Enaero II]]: 27,968 gil
*[[Enstone II]]: 26,112 gil
*[[Enthunder II]]: 25,600 gil
*[[Enwater II]]: 33,000 gil
*[[Refresh II]]: 150,000 gil

'''Note:''' There is a ticker that ticks every second that reduces her earnings. To change from Lv1 to Lv2 stall, you need to buy 10k+ worth of stuff from her and wait 50min hour then buy a little from her again. Similarly, you need to buy 250k+ worth of items from her after she levels up and wait for 50min again and buy a bunch of stuff from her again so she can level up. It is unknown at the moment how much gil per second is reduced. (source: Final Fantasy XI Guild Masters Guide Ver.101207 ISBN-10: 4797362294)

If you buy items from her, and in doing so make her stock change, she will say the following: "My new shipment has finally come in. Talk to me, and I can show you what we have!"

*Batallia Downs: 2 Cardians
*Rolanberry Fields: 3 Cardians
*Sauromugue Champaign: 3 Cardians
The Cardians live just outside the exits from Jeuno. As the name implies, their intended purpose is to allow players to test combat macros that are only usable during combat.
* Check as "Impossible to Gauge".
* Do not move or fight back.
* Damage from all attacks (both physical and magical) is reduced to zero.
* Completely immune to all enfeebles except [[Dia]] and [[Bio]] (damage over time from those two spells is also reduced to zero).
* You cannot gain TP and you cannot gain combat or magic skillups from attacking them.
* Their HP is shrouded at all times.

Like Domain Invasion, Macro Test cardians can be attacked by any player regardless of party or alliance formation. Unlike Domain Invasion, Trusts can not be called out while engaged with a Macro Test cardian. You can disengage and immediately begin calling trusts.
